answer: Each of 124 aliases needs its own meeting minutes, and the years behind each one make bulk forgery cost more than the reward. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. A school governor tenure with board meeting minutes works as the gate: minutes signed across years on one governing board. The shale is the bottleneck and the quartz is the receipt: a farm must clear both for each of its 124 aliases, the signal trail is public, and one honest agent clears them once.
